brief: Goldman's Washington Politics team ties a widening Democratic generic-ballot lead (8.5pp on September 30, now 8.9%) to rising US gasoline prices, which spiked at the onset of the Iran war, eased back over summer, and are climbing again amid tanker mine strikes in the Strait of Hormuz and Hurricane Isaias cutting 63% of Gulf offshore oil output. That lead pushes House control to a near-lock (29 Republican-held districts under Trump's 12pp 2024 margin, Democrats favored in 25) and lifts prediction-market odds of a Democratic Senate majority to 65%, with Ohio the marginal 51st seat. Goldman's own historical work on past midterms (2002-2022) finds challenger sweep odds typically fade about 5 percentage points into Election Day, implying roughly 58% rather than 63-65%, and finds a stronger partisan lean in recent red-state Senate polling (R² 0.65 for 2018-2022) that could understate Republican support in Ohio, Maine, Iowa, Kansas, Texas and Alaska. Republican Senate spending overtook Democrats only in September. BofA's Hartnett separately expects a sweep to trigger a stock slump, hedged with short financials and the dollar.
